# Chapter Eight: Silvan Politics

Corliss stood at the railing watching as the four Silvan soldiers mounted the strange ballista to the reinforced rails looking down upon the forest floor. She had seen them install at least four of these same models, but they were odd with what looked like a drum where she would normally see the large arrow prepped to fire. “What are you still doing here?” Uri asked as he came to stand next to her. He had been in session with Durass and the council all morning leaving her to explore the vast city in the trees.

I walked around for awhile, but I get the distinct impression there aren’t a lot of Silvan’s who want us here” she responded eyeing two civilians as they passed them, the two women giving the wardens a very cold stare. Corliss matched it, waiting until the women dropped their gaze, this place might be beautifull, but the people could use a lesson in being good hosts she thought. Uri followed her eyes noticing the citizens as they passed. “Understand they have not seen people outside of their own kind for generations, its normal for them to be a little wary of us” he commented gently. Corliss understood, doesn’t mean she liked it, the entire day had been spent wandering the large city with people giving her looks or whispering behind her back, every vibe that she received was either hostile or cold.

Turning back to the large Balista or whatever it was she nodded at it. “What is that thing?” she asked Uri who looked towards it and smiled. “While our people spent many generations concentrating on Magic and sacrificing innovation in order areas, the Silvan’s did not they are much more advanced in a lot of ways and that includes defense and weapons then we are or were” he finished and Corliss nodded the comment still not answering her question but it at least gave her context. “Come on, Durass wishes to meet with us” he said motioning for Corliss to join him.

She followed as he began to navigate through the city, passing the large city hall where they had gotten there official welcome and entry into the city they walked behind the building to a row of ornate houses that were reserved for government officials, finally coming to one that had a large flag with a crest on it. Uri went to the door and using the large brass ring on it, slammed it a few times before an older woman opened up, smiling at Uri she moved out of the way letting the two in. Corliss eyed the woman as the two passed into the foyer, she looked matronly and was definitely much older than Durass, her stance and demeanor spoke servant Corliss assuming she was the house mother or maid. Many lords had such women in the territories who ran their house so finding one here wasn’t a surprise.

The foyer however was incredible she thought, the bannisters were all rounded and hand carved and the wainscoting was detailed with large forest scenes. Where most of the wood in her world was blocky and utilitarian, everything here was contoured and rounded as if someone had carved every inch of the house instead of just building it. She felt at a loss to truly describe the feeling of walking into such a place as if every detail outshined any home or property, she had ever entered including some of the most ornate castles in existence within the territories. “This is amazing” she breathed her eyes wide as she tried to take in every detail. “Thank you, we take pride in our artisans here” came a familiar voice from the staircase as Durass slowly descended, gliding more then walking as he finally touched down on the foyer granite floor his smile warm as he welcomed the two low landers. “Thank you for coming, we have much to discuss” he said motioning for them to follow him as he walked deeper into the large estate. The same comfortable and ornate dark wood accompanied the small group as they walked deeper into the large house, finally coming to Durass’s private office. He showed them in, closing the door behind Uri. “We have reports of Warden’s keep being reinforced, my advisors believe it is a prelude to an assault on the northern border. I tend to agree” he began motioning them over to the table where a large map had been laid out. “we are currently reinforcing the defences in the city as you have seen, but we are also going to be adding new defenses throughout the forest leading up from the southern border. I know we have refugees coming up and my people will be there to meet them. I would also like some of the warden’s there as well” he began showing the two the large map with the border areas clearly marked as well as notes on the keep and the current defenses. “The reason I would like Wardens to accompany my scouts is that when people see us for the first time, it can be a little unsettling and with the reports coming out of the territory of the white wraiths, some people are automatically fighting off my scouts” he finished shaking his head. “Its not making our ability to take in your people easier my friend” he admitted, and Uri nodded gravely. Corliss looked over the map eyeing the notes on the keep which included what looked like up to date numbers on soldiers. “Looking at these numbers it appears we are talking two entire regiments that are currently there” she breathed, wondering what the Empress was to, that was almost an invasion force she thought looking over the defenses of the city. Durass nodded “There is another regiment on the way as well, whatever they are planning will quite probably happen within the month” he announced, and Corliss winced at the thought of the death and desctruction that would follow an invasion of that level.

“The reason I called you two in” Durass began, focusing their attention to the woods that lay between the border and the city. “Is I am putting together a contingent to mine and trap the areas in the forest leading up to the city, I don’t want to offer the soldiers any place they can rest or make camp, the goal is not only to harass and thin their lines but also ensure that any encampment is well away from the city ensuring long marches should they wish to assault this place” he said and both Uri and Corliss nodded. They had come through the forest, it was dense with little area to camp, mine and trap it effectively it will make traveling difficult for the invaders and also ensure any rear guard stays near the border. “Okay, we can do that” Corliss stated looking up at the general who seemed to breath a sigh of relief. “There is a lot going on and with the oncoming invasion, people are scared, the less they see of low landers, the better it will be” he finally admitted, and Corliss could see the shame on the man’s face. She understood it completely, he knew the different between friend of foe, but to most of the Silvans who had never been in the presence of Low Landers would lump them together she could already feel the zenophobic air taking hold in the streets.

“There is something else” he began looking over a few of the notes on the map. “The Empress has platoons and Mages scouring the land, she is looking for someone, according to our reports he is a man who fell from the sky and so far has eluded the Empress, but she is incredibly interested in finding him.” He finished looking up at the two and noticed Corlisses eyes when he mentioned it she looked up to see the General eyeing her questioningly and shaking her head decided there was no point in keeping it hidden. “I was asked to find something that fell from the sky, I later found out it was a person, I was not successful but it sounds like the Empress is still engaged in that search” she began Durass reguarding her as he worked through his own thoughts. “At the very least it will distract her from invading” she said and then shook her head as Durass was about to speak. “The next question you will ask is going to disappoint you General, I have no idea why the Empress wants him and aside from some basic information nothing I know eludes to who he is” she finished and Durass smiled at her “We have a lot of reports and are unsure what to believe, I am afraid my people might be embellishing them somewhat” he said embarrassed. Both Uri and Corliss looked to the general “Why would your people embellish information?” Uri beat her to it, but both continued to look at him curiously as Durass winced a little, still looking embarrassed.

We have an old legend, more of a superstition actually of one who will be sent from the heavens, one of the ancients who will lead out people into the next age, the age, this will be an ancient of the old power and old values” he said and shot them a sheepish look. Its an origin story, basically they say one of those like the people who created us will return” he finished almost apologetically. “Its still a story that is told to the young and even the old sometimes reference it. Somewhere along the line someone made the association so now there are those who believe this man is sky touched” he finished referencing an ancient term for those blessed by the gods.

Uri shook his head “I get hope, but they might be disappointed should this man be discovered by the Empress Durass, it is likely she will kill him” he finished and Durass winced. “There are rumors he is headed north my friend, should he make it, I fear some of my people might follow him, and I don’t know if that would be a good thing or not” he finished and Corliss could see the concern on his face. A lowlander with the power to command Silvan’s would be dangerous she thought to herself. If that man made it north, she would have to watch him carefully, should he try and take advantage of that situation, she might be forced to end him for all their sakes. Looking to Uri she could see he had a similar thought and subtly she nodded to him.

They finished up and headed out of the house. Uri and Corliss reported to the main common area where a group of Silvan scouts stood awaiting them. Boxes and packs stuffed with various items were hoisted onto backs and carried between them as in small groups they entered the elevator and descended to the forest floor. All in All, twelve wardens joined twenty of the Silvan scouts as they marched back towards the territory border.

Once there the scouts began unpacking small packs and spools of wire, laying them out carefully on the ground. “What is that?” Corliss asked trying to get a better look at the set of items. One of the scouts smiled at her “Its an explosive pack” he stated, opening it and showing her the dull brown brick which looked like thick mud and the two crystals buried in it. “It’s a composition made up of certain tree saps, crystal resin and a few minerals, combine that with the two crystals that act as a blasting source, the wires hold the crystals apart, once a wire is broken the explosive detonates” he finished, showing her how to attach the wire to the spring loaded crystals that were held apart with a piece of tree bark, once he had attacked it to a tree and strung the wire taught, he attacked the string to one of the crystals and removed the tree bark, showing them step by step how to do it. “Now its armed, don’t break the wire, or you will be having a very bad day” he said smiling at the group of wardens.

For safety each warden was paired with a Silvan scout, while the warden’s ran the wire the Silvans set and armed the explosive. They spent the entire afternoon walking quadrants and setting the impromptu booby traps, ensuring to carefully mark each one on the map while leaving a clear path back to the city, that anyone who knew where to find the explosive could easily lead people to the city, but those without that knowledge would quickly find themselves walking into a trap. The small group returned to the city a short time later, Corliss approached the elevator which now had sandbags surrounding it and two more of those strange weapons mounted on either side.

As she approached her ride back into the city, she could hear a commotion coming from the common area above, but they were too far to make out any of the words. Curiously the entire group looked up trying to gage what was happening. “That’s not good” she said, and Uri looked at her, giving her a meaningful glance “I have a feeling we are involved even if its not directly” he said, and Corliss looked at her master seeing the worried look in his eyes. She wasn’t sure she wanted to go back up, not if they were walking into a full-blown riot she thought, thankfully one of the scouts took care of that. “Why don’t you all stay here, I am going to go up and see whats going on, don’t come up until I come down and get you” he said Corliss thinking he had the same idea as Uri. With a nod the group spread out a bit, finding places to sit and rest while they listened to the continuing commotion above. Corliss sat in the shadow of the city listening to the noise filtering down, they were far enough away that that voices simply merged together sounding more like a wave against the shore instead of a riot or argument. After an hour the solder returned his face was pale as he walked to the center of the small group, everyone sitting up and giving him his attention. The look on his face wasn’t good she thought leaning forward.

“The second Regiment has reached the fort, according to our scouts the army is preparing to march, people are scared” he simply said turning to take a seat with the rest of them. Corliss cocked her head at him “Okay, why are we staying down here?” she asked looking towards the elevator and a bath. The soldier shook his head “Better to wait until it dies down, seeing a lowlander wouldn’t be the best thing right now. General Durass asks that we wait a while and he will retrieve us once everyone has calmed” the soldiers said, and Corliss sat back.

That did not bode well she thought. Continuing to listen to the roar of the crowds above. She and Uri had come here, had trusted Durass with the Warden’s safety more and more that decision was looking like a bad one she thought. They were going to need an exit strategy if this continued, she mused watching the other wardens as they glanced upward, the discomfort and fear on there face evident. These were men and women who had been raised with the respect of there position, they were not used to being treated like pariah’s it was killing moral and worse, instilling self doubt in the lot of them. “Alright, if they are going to fight, we are going to do something productive, Wardens gather up we are going to scout the area” she said, knowing it was makework but needing to give something to the wardens to do. They slowly moved and gathered up, getting their gear as the soldiers looked at them curiously.

Corliss shot an acidic look to the commander of the soldiers contingent and he nodded, sitting back. At least he understands what I am trying to do she thought turning to the wardens. Corliss quickly went to work setting assignments and splitting out Recon groups and it wasn’t long after that she found hersleft knee deep in the brush navigating the traps and walking a perimeter. Listening she could hear the light sound further in the forest as other groups of wardens did the same. Everyone was spread far enough to cover and area but close enough to raise an alarm should they need to.

“Commander, I would think with the traps and such that this is not necessary” whispered one of her bowmen, koplir she thought his name was, turning she reguarded him cooly. “So, you think the enemy is so easily fooled that they would simply walk into a trap and then go home?” he asked arching an eyebrow. Koplir winced as heard the reproachfull tone in his commander’s voice and shook his head. “No, your right” he said doing his best to pull his foot out of his mouth, but Corliss had already dismissed the comment, her attention was focused on the distant horizon, about two hundred feet past the end of the woods the border for the territories began and her homeland of Vicor. Somewhere over there came the distant beating of hooves she thought, stopping the group and studying the land. With a motion the group dropped fluidly into a crouch, the edges of the group point weapons out while everyone kept one eye on the Commander, crouching there Corliss closed her eyes and held her breath, trying to force the noises of the forest away and instead concentrate on the hill. Slowly opening her eyes, she watched, silently waiting as the hoof beats increased in volume slightly.

Whatever was coming, was headed this way she thought. Turning to the Koplis who had setup on her right, his rifle trained steadily out into the forest. With a nod and a confirmation, he let out a mournful whistle, a moment later it was returned as the warning was passed down the line. Further in the wood’s groups would be crouching and holding, preparing as they waited to find out what the warning was. Corliss did not have to worry about them getting impatient or jumping up to gain glory, these were Wardens, they had been trained since children to hunt and kill, they would not disappoint. Training her eyes on the hill Corliss went still simply watching and breathing as she waited to understand the oncoming threat, she was not scared nor anxious, she did not figit but instead crouched like a stone, stalwart in her thoughts as he concentrated on her vision. Watching the rolling hill, something finally changed and as she studied the terrain three people broke over the top of the hill, two carrying a third she marked. They made it halfway down the hill, slowed by the person who was being dragged as the Empresss guard on horseback emerged from over the hill. “They aren’t going to make it” Corliss hissed and with a motion started her patrol moving towards the edge of the forest, the whistle went out along the patrols as they began to reposition and move, the woods were quiet despite the activity.

Once she was in position, she marked the three as they approached, now she could see the three clearly, two woman, one young and one old carrying a young man, all three were dressed like mages she noticed, squinting to get a better look.

The soldiers knew they were mages as well she thought, watching as they approached and then dropped back trying to force the two mages to use their power. Despite what most people understood Mages did not have a never-ending supply and ability, each use of the gift, wore on them ultimately making them too exaughsted to cast. The soldiers were testing them she noticed narrowing her eyes to watch them.

As they drew closer, she could see the hopelessness in the older woman’s eyes, she knew what they were doing, understood that the two of them were defencless and weren’t going to make it. It was a powerful moment for Corliss, she had the power of life or death and before she could weigh the conceqences of her actions, she moved the directive to help, to protect so much a part of her, she didn’t even hesitate. With a motion the team was moving, bursting through the brush as they rushed to leave the protection of the woods. The soldiers were busy concentrating on the mages they didn’t even see the group until the first blue streams of energy slammed into the two closest.

The commander’s head shot up and he pointed, the soldiers had been riding and trying to take the small group alive Corliss thought, there guns were slung and now they worked to remove them from there shoulders and saddle holsters, but before they had the chance, one after another they quickly dropped to the steady shooting of Wardens. Finally, the field was quiet except for the sound of retreating, riderless horses and Corliss approached the small group, the three had collapsed onto the ground once the shoot had begun. The older woman, her chest heading, and her silver hair strewn about from the exertion “Thank you” she whispered to Corliss who smiled and nodded. The young woman was covering the unconscious man with her body, Corliss reguarded her, could see the eyes shift, she loved this man, would die before she would allow any of her people to hurt him.

Corliss was taken aback, as a woman she found this incredible and sad at the same time, she had never felt such a powerful emotion and yet it obviously existed because here was proof, a small pang of jealousy for this woman sprung up but she quickly squashed it, why should she feel resentment towards this woman because Corliss herself had never found someone who made her feel like that.

Kneeling down she pulled her hands away from her weapons, extending them out in front of her she locked eyes with the young woman, her raven hair half covering the intense blue eyes beneath. “We will not hurt him, but I want my medic to take a look, is that okay?” she asked keeping her tone gentle as she did. The girl’s eyes shot from soldier to soldier and then down to the young man and Corliss could see the tears welling as she noticed his contidion they had probably been running and trying to escape she had not noticed just how bad he was. Finally looking up at her, she simply nodded, and Corliss made a motion. One of the wardens came over and began to gently prod the unconious man.

“The older woman looked over and eyed the soldier working on the unconscious man. “Soldier, what is his condition” she asked, and the voice held authority, the authority of someone who was used to being deferred to in situations like this. The soldier without missing a beat or looking up began to speak solfty as he pulled out bandages and salves. “I need to stabilize him, he is in bad shape, I am guessing multiple broken bones, swelling of the brain and internet bleeding, but he is alive” he said continuing to work. The woman crawled over to the man and began examining him. “Are you a doctor?” Corliss finally asked and the woman simply nodded. “I need to get him someplace safe and soon, I need a hospital where I can work” she said, locking eyes with Corliss aand she could see the pleading in those eyes. With a nod, she motioned out the other teams. “Get me a gourny, I need it asap, we are brining him back with us” she finished, and the soldiers hesitated. Corliss knew why, these were mages, the Empress had been using Mages to enforce her new order and Silvan’s were already touchy. She shot him an annoyed look and he simply nodded taking off into the woods with two others. Politics be damned she thought resolving that she would not leave people to die simply to make a politician’s life easer.

She stood there watching the two work on the young man, her team spread out to cover the field as they continied to try and stabilize him. Finally, the soldier returned with two long branches and cloth strung between them. They gently laid it down next to the man and with the supervision of the Mage Doctor and the medic, they moved him and lifted him gently. The entire group dissolved into the treeline making their way back towards the city. Corliss followed the precession keeping behind the man being carried as the older woman joined her, walking in silence for a few moments before speaking. “I wanted to thank you for saving us” She began, and Corliss made a motion for her to stop. “Its what we do, but I don’t know how the reception of more lowlanders will be to the Silvan’s” she said, and the woman simply nodded. “The Silvan’s have always been a bit zenophobic, but the order does have some dealings with them so I am hoping that goodwill can be implied upon, this once” she said smiling weakly. Corliss looked at the woman she did not know anyone had dealings with the Silvan’s but apparently, they had kept in contact with the mages at least. She filed that away for later and continued to walk. “I am Master Patrice, and this is Initiate Dara, the man you carry is Marcus Gavin” she said looking at Marcus as he laid unconscious in front of them.

“I am Warden Corliss” she said and Patrice nodded “We had heard the Wardens had traveled North abandoning the keep” she said, it was not an accusation nor was there any heat in the statement, it was simply a statement so Corliss did not try to defend it. She instead focused on the woman’s introduction, she had not given the man on the gourney a title, but Corliss spied the clothes, he was dressed as a mage. “Is that man not a mage?” she asked pointing to Marcus. She was quiet as Patrice reguarded him and finally turned her head to look at Corliss. “He is, but not of the order. His story is different, but understand he is special and there are those who hunt for him, our only choice was to come here” she said Corliss nodding and looking back at the man they carried.

What kind of trouble do you bring us Marcus she wondered as the city came into view?
